If you only remember one thing: Anthropic just detailed a nearly two hundred million interaction campaign by five China based A I labs to distill Claude's capabilities into their own models. It's the clearest sign yet that the U S China A I rivalry has moved from chips to the models themselves.

Section one. A I and models.

Anthropic's new threat intelligence report names Alibaba, Moonshot A I, DeepSeek, Xiaomi, and Zhipu as running what it calls illicit distillation campaigns, feeding Claude's outputs into their own training pipelines without permission. Alibaba's campaign alone generated more than one hundred fifty one million Claude interactions between May and July, spread across roughly three thousand five hundred flagged accounts. Moonshot took a sneakier approach, routing some Kimi user requests to Claude, then presenting Claude's answers as its own. Your Rundown newsletter is covering the same story from the bad actors versus Claude angle.

On the release side, it's a crowded week. Sakana A I shipped Fugu Ultra version two and Fugu Max, DeepSeek pushed out version four point one Flash, and Google DeepMind released Gemini three point eight Flash, plus a restricted sibling, Gemini three point eight Flash Cyber, that comes with extra access and logging requirements. OpenAI, meanwhile, paused new sign ups for its two hundred dollar Pro tier on G P T six Astra because of system strain. Existing subscribers are unaffected. Your Batch newsletter frames it as Astra and Claude Fable five point one fighting for the top leaderboard spot, while Microsoft, Google, and Meta all quietly shipped new speech to text models this week.

Why it matters: the fight over whose model can copy whose is now just as consequential as the fight over whose chips are faster.

Section two. A I ethics and policy.

California Governor Newsom signed a package of what's being called the strongest child safety A I and social media laws in the country. Platforms can't offer addictive feeds to anyone under sixteen. A I chatbots must disclose they're not human. Companies must run risk assessments before launching chatbots. And negligent harm to a child can now cost up to one million dollars per case. Separately, Microsoft published its twenty twenty six Responsible A I Transparency Report on governance and red teaming, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology put out draft guidance on using A I within its cybersecurity framework. The E U's A I Act is also fully biting now. Any team building, buying, or selling A I needs documented risk classification and human oversight on record.

Why it matters: regulation is catching up fastest where kids are involved. Expect other states to copy California's playbook.

Section three. Tech geopolitics.

Chip policy has quietly loosened. The Commerce Department shifted Nvidia's H two hundred licensing to China from presumptive denial to case by case approval, with mandatory U S based third party testing, a cap at half of domestic shipment volume, and a twenty five percent tariff per shipment. The once solid bipartisan consensus on chip restrictions has splintered into a three way standoff between Congress, the White House, and the chip industry itself. That loosening sits oddly next to the Anthropic distillation report from section one. Washington is easing hardware controls even as a U S lab accuses Chinese competitors of siphoning model capability directly.

Why it matters: the export control front is softening just as the model copying front heats up. The contest is shifting, not cooling.

Section four. Also worth knowing, media industry.

Your Noosphere newsletter is calling out a subtle, yet seismic shift underway in media. And your A I Collective newsletter connects three recent A I lab departures, Coxon over the competitive race, Sharma over institutional drift, and Hitzig over ads, arguing the coverage gave each one a different reason when there may be a single common thread. Worth a skim given your comms lens.

Section five. Tech for good close.

Mercy Corps is rebranding this month to Prosper Global. That's the top of the news. Your full briefing is in the recording.
